solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One authorised bonus given to workers

parts.note: a tip is a bonus payment for service
the staff are the workers of a firm

explanation.surface: A firm hands a bonus to its employees.
explanation.walkthrough: A tipstaff is a court official or sheriff's officer, someone with authority to act for the court.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is an officer empowered by a court, so the word names a person holding official authority.

clue.text: Cheese-coated food, primarily ungarnished?

parts.note: something coated in a cheese is in it
Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word food is kept

parts.note: the first letter of food

explanation.surface: A dish of food baked in cheese is hardly plain or ungarnished.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheese-coated food is food sitting IN BRIE, with the food cut to its initial. The definition is loose: speaking briefly means speaking without decoration, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something said briefly is put plainly, without embellishing detail, which the setter likens to being served without trimmings.

clue.text: Bond eats one piece of bread

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside itself, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: to solder is to bond metal
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: James Bond eating a slice of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond is not 007 but the verb, joining metals.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier is a narrow strip of toast or bread, dipped into a boiled egg; a British nursery usage.

clue.text: I can see that odd number

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the whole phrase is the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a figure looks peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: Read number as numb-er, a thing that numbs, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaesthetic deadens feeling, so it is literally something that numbs, a numb-er.

clue.text: Much about turning behind to medium size here?

definitions.text: Much about turning behind to medium size here?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the next

parts.note: far as in far better, by much

indicators.note: turning round makes the word behind run in the opposite direction

parts.note: aft is the nautical word for behind
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A big backside being slimmed down to an average size.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi-&lit: the whole clue pictures reducing a large behind to medium size at a health resort, so the wordplay words double as the picture of the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A fat farm is a slimming resort where overweight people go to lose weight, so it is where a big rear end is cut down.

clue.text: Simple house with parking on A1

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
re means on or concerning
A1 means first-rate, as does fab

explanation.surface: A modest home with parking, located on the A1 road.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 looks like Britain's longest road, but it is A1 meaning excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a prefabricated building, a quickly assembled and basic dwelling, as built in Britain after the war.

clue.text: Turning left and right, less important sort of wheel

indicators.note: turning here means the letter for left and the letter for right trade places in the word

parts.note: lower in rank means less important

explanation.surface: A minor wheel that swivels both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the L at the front of LOWER with the R at the end to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowel is the small spiked revolving wheel on the end of a rider's spur.

clue.text: Smoking group completely stop

parts.note: FOREST is the Freedom Organisation for the Right to Enjoy Smoking Tobacco, a British pro-smoking lobby
all means completely, as in all gone

explanation.surface: A gathering of smokers decides to give up entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: FOREST is a British smokers' rights campaign group, not trees.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to prevent something by acting first, which is to stop it happening.

clue.text: Lecture about a small level of interest

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps round what follows

parts.note: to berate is to lecture angrily
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A talk on some minor topic that hardly anyone cares about.
explanation.walkthrough: Level of interest sounds like boredom, but it is the bank's lending rate.
explanation.definitionFit: The base rate is the central bank's benchmark interest rate, from which lenders set their own percentages.

clue.text: Lincoln Cathedral's last murder victim

parts.note: Abe Lincoln, the US president

indicators.note: last points to the final letter only of the word Cathedral

parts.note: the final letter of Cathedral

explanation.surface: The final killing at Lincoln Cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln is the president, not the English city with the cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Abel was killed by his brother Cain, the first murder victim in the Bible.

clue.text: Wanting charges later

parts.note: to be after something is to want it
wards are people in someone's charge

explanation.surface: Someone wants to bring charges at a later date.
explanation.definitionFit: Afterwards and later are synonyms, both meaning at a subsequent time.

clue.text: One very bright teacher is blocked by university

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir

indicators.note: something blocked by another has it stuck in its middle, so one piece sits inside

parts.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A brilliant teacher finds the university standing in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Very bright suggests a clever person, but it is literal brightness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the Dog Star, is the brightest star in the night sky.

clue.text: Nearly as upset as one breaking down

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: both words form the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone almost as distressed as a person having a breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: Breaking down suggests collapse in tears; here it means dissecting into parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An analyser breaks things down into their components to examine them.

clue.text: Concept car safety feature — grip

parts.note: ABS is an anti-lock braking system
traction is a tyre's grip on the road

explanation.surface: A concept car's safety system is all about grip.
explanation.walkthrough: Concept car reads as one phrase, but Concept is the definition and car begins the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstraction is an idea considered apart from concrete things, a general notion.

clue.text: Usually on top, master criminal

parts.note: forth means on or onward, as in from this day forth

indicators.note: criminal means crooked or bent, so the letters are twisted into another order

parts.note: the two words form the fodder

explanation.surface: As a rule, a mastermind of crime stays on top.
explanation.walkthrough: Master criminal reads as a mastermind; master is fodder and criminal the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: For the most part is an idiom meaning generally or in most cases, the same as usually.

clue.text: Attack that may cause wounding

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a military assault, as a noun
second meaning: insulting, hurtful to feelings

explanation.walkthrough: Wounding reads as physical injury in a battle, but the second sense is hurt feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a military campaign of attack and an adjective for remarks that hurt or insult.

clue.text: She dared to cook ducks

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the two words form the fodder

explanation.surface: A woman bravely attempts to roast some ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: Ducks could be a verb, dodging; here it is the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The redhead is a North American diving duck whose drake has a chestnut head.

clue.text: Some odd issue of Paris Match?

definitions.text: Some odd issue of Paris Match?

parts.words: Some odd issue of Paris Match?
parts.note: surface reading: a strange edition of the French news magazine Paris Match

parts.words: Some odd issue of Paris Match?
parts.note: setter's reading: issue is offspring, and a Paris match is a French marriage, so a badly behaved child, said in French

explanation.walkthrough: Issue means children and match means a marriage; the French phrase names a badly behaved child, or a shocking young talent.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase, literally a terrible child, is used for an unruly youngster or provocative newcomer, an odd offspring of a French union.

clue.text: Old Paddy set up foreign trade?

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: in a down entry set up means raised upward, so the word runs bottom to top

parts.note: a paddy is a tantrum, as is a strop, in British slang

explanation.surface: An Irishman of old established overseas commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy looks like an Irishman, but it is a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Exports are goods sold abroad, the outbound side of foreign trade, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Save a great deal for servant

parts.note: save and but both mean except
tons means lots

explanation.surface: Putting aside a large sum of money to pay a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: Save looks like a verb about money; it is the preposition meaning except. Buttons is the pageboy in the Cinderella pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttons is the traditional nickname for a pageboy, from the rows of buttons on his uniform.

clue.text: Copy one bird and others will come back

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless bird

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way it came, so the phrase is read from its end

parts.note: et al is Latin shorthand for and others

explanation.surface: If one bird mimics, the rest of the flock will follow back.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate is to imitate someone admired, a synonym of copy as a verb.

clue.text: Block letters after G better

parts.note: H and I are the letters following G, read as H AND I
to cap is to better or outdo

explanation.surface: Instructions for writing capitals after the letter G in a better style.
explanation.walkthrough: Block letters suggests capitals; Block is the definition and letters after G are spelled out with the word and between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To handicap is to hinder or impede, which is to block someone's progress.

clue.text: Clumsy writer about to get into it

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An awkward author is just about to start on a piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill, so an inept person is awkward or clumsy.

clue.text: Copper market's failed

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to tout is to market or sell

explanation.surface: The copper market has collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: Market is a verb here, to sell; 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that cuts out stops working, so the phrase means failed or stalled.

clue.text: I have to fill potty carried for so long

indicators.note: filling something means going inside it
potty means crazy, so the letters go haywire into a new order

parts.note: the fodder word
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone has to fill a child's potty they have been carrying for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: Potty is the toilet seat in the surface but means mad here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian farewell means until we see each other again, the same parting as so long.

clue.text: Stone work filling in wall

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: the filling in something is its middle, so only the inner letters of wall are kept

parts.note: the middle two letters of wall

explanation.surface: A job of stuffing a gap in a stone wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a gemstone, prized for its shifting play of colours.

clue.text: Cosiest area to catch some sleep

indicators.note: to catch is to hold inside, so the run of letters is held within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: The snuggest spot in which to grab a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap, a short spell of sleep.

clue.text: Is in heat — that's ominous

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next word

parts.note: to sinter is to heat powdered material until it fuses
taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal in heat behaves in a way that seems menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: In heat suggests an animal in season; heat is the verb sinter, a metalworking term.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means threatening harm, which is what ominous means too.
